concepts.title: Elements of a Triangle
concepts.definition: A triangle has 6 elements: 3 sides and 3 angles. The side opposite to vertex A is BC. Triangles are classified by sides (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) and by angles (acute, obtuse, right).
concepts.key_idea: Triangle has 3 sides, 3 angles. Classified by sides and angles.
question_patterns: write the six elements of triangle

solution_steps.explain: List the 3 sides
List the 3 angles
By sides: scalene (all different), isosceles (2 equal), equilateral (all equal). By angles: acute (all < 90), obtuse (one > 90), right (one = 90).

concepts.title: Medians of a Triangle
concepts.definition: A median connects a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side. A triangle has 3 medians.
concepts.formula: median = vertex to midpoint of opposite side; 3 medians per triangle
concepts.key_idea: Median joins vertex to midpoint of opposite side. 3 medians.
question_patterns: how many medians can a triangle have

solution_steps.explain: Locate midpoint of opposite side
Connect vertex to midpoint
There are 3 medians, one from each vertex

concepts.title: Altitudes of a Triangle
concepts.definition: An altitude is a perpendicular line segment from a vertex to the opposite side (or line containing it). A triangle has 3 altitudes.
concepts.formula: altitude = perpendicular from vertex to opposite side; 3 altitudes
concepts.key_idea: Altitude is perpendicular from vertex to opposite side. 3 altitudes.

solution_steps.explain: Choose a vertex

Altitude may be inside (acute), on (right), or outside (obtuse) the triangle

concepts.title: Exterior Angle Property
concepts.definition: An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two interior opposite angles. exterior = interior1 + interior2.
concepts.key_idea: Exterior angle = sum of two interior opposite angles.

solution_steps.explain: Find the exterior angle (formed by extending a side)

If one angle is unknown, subtract known from exterior

concepts.title: Angle Sum Property
concepts.definition: The sum of the three angles of a triangle is 180 degrees. angle1 + angle2 + angle3 = 180.
concepts.key_idea: Three angles of a triangle always sum to 180 degrees.

concepts.title: Equilateral Triangle
concepts.definition: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal and each angle measures 60 degrees.
concepts.formula: all sides equal; each angle = 60 degrees
concepts.key_idea: All sides equal, all angles 60 degrees.
question_patterns: explain equilateral triangle with an example

solution_steps.explain: All three sides must be equal
Each angle = 60 degrees

concepts.title: Isosceles Triangle
concepts.definition: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides. The base angles (angles opposite to equal sides) are equal.
concepts.formula: two sides equal; base angles equal
concepts.key_idea: Two equal sides, two equal base angles.
question_patterns: find angles x and y in isosceles

solution_steps.explain: Find which two sides are equal
Angles opposite to equal sides are equal
If vertex angle known, base_angle = (180 - vertex_angle) / 2

concepts.title: Sum of Two Sides of Triangle
concepts.definition: The sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle is greater than the third side. The difference of any two sides is less than the third side.
concepts.formula: a + b > c; |a - b| < c for all sides
concepts.key_idea: Sum of any two sides > third side. Difference < third side.

concepts.title: Pythagoras Theorem
concepts.definition: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares on the legs. a^2 = b^2 + c^2 where a is hypotenuse.
concepts.key_idea: Square of hypotenuse = sum of squares of other two sides.

solution_steps.explain: Find which angle is 90 degrees
Side opposite to right angle is hypotenuse
hypotenuse^2 = leg1^2 + leg2^2
If finding hypotenuse: h = sqrt(leg1^2 + leg2^2). If finding leg: leg = sqrt(h^2 - other_leg^2)

concepts.title: Converse of Pythagoras
concepts.definition: If the square of one side equals the sum of squares of the other two sides, then the triangle is right-angled. The right angle is opposite the longest side.
concepts.formula: if a^2 = b^2 + c^2, then right-angled with hypotenuse a
concepts.key_idea: If Pythagoras holds, triangle is right-angled.
question_patterns: determine if triangle is right angled

solution_steps.explain: Identify the longest side
longest^2 = side1^2 + side2^2?
If yes, right-angled with right angle opposite longest side. If no, not right-angled.
